agent: iostream-tail: the nine addresses the two log waves still reached into
question: 0x794A6E and 0x795991 (handed over as 'the two halves of building the std::ios_base::failure that ios_base::clear throws'), 0x794AE9 (uncaught_exception), 0x794AEE (ios_base::_Callfns), 0x2EE40 (std::locale::~locale), 0x79504A/0x795072 (_Lockit ctor/dtor), 0x920940 (the real basic_stringbuf::str) and 0x2210 (the ios_base scalar deleting destructor). Confirm or refute each rather than landing the handed-over label; give what it does, its signature and calling convention read off the ret and the call sites, and a name or a plain statement that it cannot be named.

addresses.name: std::iostream_category
addresses.comment:
**Two instructions - `mov eax, 0x16F5204; ret` - and it is not half of building the exception.** It is `std::iostream_category()`: the address it answers is the static `_Iostream_error_category` singleton, whose vfptr at `+0` is `0x15A7A84` and whose RTTI type descriptor reads `.?AV_Iostream_error_category@std@@`. Its `name()` (slot 1, `0x794A66`) is `return *(const char**)(this+4)`, and `this+4` = `0x16F5204+4` holds `0x15A7A74`, the address of the literal `"iostream"`.

The three call sites are the three throw paths of `std::ios_base::clear` (`0x20B0`) and each uses the result as the `_Cat` half of an `error_code`:

    call  std::iostream_category         ; edi = the category
    mov   [esp+0xC], 0x15B4E4C           ; "ios_base::badbit set"
    lea   ecx, [esp+0x10]                ; the exception object
    call  std::exception::exception      ; 0x795991
    mov   [esp+0x20], esi                ; error_code._Val  = 1  (io_errc::stream)
    mov   [esp+0x24], edi                ; error_code._Cat  = this
    mov   [esp+0x14], 0x15A7BD8          ; vfptr <- std::ios_base::failure
    call  _CxxThrowException

So `ios_base::clear` throws `failure(msg, make_error_code(io_errc::stream))`, exactly as `<xiosbase>` documents, and the `failure` layout is {vfptr, `_Mywhat`, `_Mydofree`, `_Mycode._Val`, `_Mycode._Cat`}. `__cdecl`, no arguments, bare `ret`, pointer back in eax. The `_Generic_error_category` and `_System_error_category` singletons sit immediately after it, at `0x16F5208` and `0x16F520C`, with tables `0x15A7A5C` and `0x15A7AA8`; their accessors and virtuals are left on the frontier.
addresses.evidence:
Mechanical, three steps, all in the image. (1) `image.read(0x16F5204,4)` is `0x15A7A84`, and the RTTI complete-object-locator four bytes before that table points at a type descriptor whose name is `.?AV_Iostream_error_category@std@@`. (2) The same table's slot 1 is `0x794A66` = `mov eax,[ecx+4]; ret`, and `image.read(0x16F5208,4)` = `0x15A7A74`, where the bytes are `iostream\0`. (3) All three callers (`findRefs --callers 0x00B94A6E`: 0x4020E8, 0x402129, 0x402165) are inside `std::ios_base::clear`, which project.json already names, and each stores the returned pointer next to the constant 1 and then throws an object whose vftable `0x15A7BD8` has RTTI `.?AVfailure@ios_base@std@@`.

What would show it wrong: `0x16F5204` not being the start of the object - if the vfptr sat elsewhere the first dword would not be a table whose RTTI names the category class; or a fourth call site that used the result as something other than an `error_category*` (there is none, `findRefs --address` finds no data reference to this function either). The handover's reading - 'one of the two halves of building the failure' - is **refuted**: the category object is not part of the exception, it is the `_Cat` member of the `error_code` the exception carries, and this function neither writes nor allocates anything.

addresses.name: std::exception::exception
addresses.signature: std::exception* __thiscall std::exception::exception(std::exception* this, const char** what) @EAX
addresses.comment:
**`std::exception::exception(const char* const& _What)`** - the base constructor of every standard exception in the image, not something built for `ios_base::failure`. It writes the `std::exception` vftable `0x15A7C88` at `+0`, zeroes `_Mywhat` at `+4` and `_Mydofree` at `+8`, then calls `_Copy_str` (`0x795933`) with `*what`.

**The parameter is a pointer to a `const char*`, not a `const char*`** - `mov eax,[ebp+8]; push [eax]` - which is MSVC's `exception(const char *const &)` signature verbatim, and is why every call site first parks the literal in a stack slot and passes that slot's address. Recording it as `const char*` would make every caller decompile with a bogus extra dereference.

`__thiscall`, `ret 4`, the object back in eax. 297 direct callers, of which the three in `std::ios_base::clear` are the ones the handover was looking at; the rest are every `throw std::runtime_error(...)` / `bad_alloc` / `bad_cast` in the game. The derived constructors are one instruction longer and sit right after it: `0x7959ED` (`bad_cast`, vftable `0x15A7CA8`), `0x795A16` (`bad_typeid`, `0x15A7CB4`), `0x402060` (`runtime_error`, `0x159FDA0`).
addresses.evidence:
(1) The vftable it writes, `0x15A7C88`, has an RTTI type descriptor reading `.?AVexception@std@@` - read straight out of the image four bytes before the table. (2) `0x795933`, the only thing it calls, is `_Copy_str`: `if (p) { n = strlen(p)+1; q = malloc(n); this->+4 = q; if (q) { strcpy_s(q,n,p); this->+8 = 1; } }`, which fixes `+4` as `_Mywhat` and `+8` as `_Mydofree`. (3) `ret 4` with `this` in ecx. (4) The `push dword ptr [eax]` on the argument is the reference-to-pointer, and the three `ios_base::clear` sites confirm it from the caller side: they write the literal into `[esp+0xC]` and pass `lea eax,[esp+8]`... the slot address, not the literal.

What would show it wrong: a caller that pushes a string literal's address directly (that would make the parameter a `const char*`) - none of the 297 that were spot-checked in `ios_base::clear` does; or `0x15A7C88` turning out not to be `std::exception`'s table, which the RTTI settles. The handover's 'one of the two halves of building the ios_base::failure' is **half right**: it is the base constructor used there, but it is a general-purpose library constructor with 297 callers and nothing about it is specific to `failure` - the `failure` vftable and the `error_code` members are written by the caller afterwards.

addresses.name: std::uncaught_exception
addresses.comment:
A five-byte `jmp 0x79CD77` and nothing else - `std::uncaught_exception()` tail-calling the CRT's `__uncaught_exception`. The handover's description is confirmed.

It has 16 callers and every one reads the result the same way, `test al,al` followed by a jump around a call: that is the `basic_ostream::sentry` destructor, `if (!uncaught_exception()) _Osfx();`. `std::ostream::write` (`0x664A30`) is the example the previous wave named - `0xA64B3B: call 0xB94AE9; test al,al; jne 0xA64B4B; mov ecx,edi; call 0x40A260`, and `0xA260` is already recorded as `std::ostream::_Osfx`.

No arguments, `bool` in al. Written `__cdecl` because the caller consumes nothing; the jump target's own `ret` is bare.
addresses.evidence:
Mechanical: the five bytes at `0xB94AE9` decode to `jmp 0xB9CD77` and nothing else; `findRefs --callers` finds 16 direct calls and no data references; the target ends in a bare `ret` with `al` set by `setne`. The reading of the call sites is mechanical too - the one at `0xA64B3B` sits inside a function project.json already records as `std::ostream::write` and guards a call to an address project.json already records as `std::ostream::_Osfx`, which is the documented body of the sentry destructor.

`inferred` rather than `confirmed` because the **name** comes from matching `<exception>` and the sentry destructor's documented body from memory, not from bytes compared against a reference build. What would show it wrong: a caller that uses the result for something other than guarding a flush or an `_Osfx` - all 16 were listed and the two inspected (`0xA64B3B`, `0xA5CBC2`) follow the pattern; or `0x79CD77` turning out to read something other than a per-thread in-flight-exception flag.

addresses.name: __uncaught_exception
addresses.comment: The CRT side of the above: `return _getptd()->_ProcessingThrow != 0`. Three instructions after the call - `call 0x7A0FFE; xor ecx,ecx; cmp [eax+0x90], ecx; setne al; ret`. `0x7A0FFE` is the per-thread data getter (59 callers across the CRT), and `+0x90` into that block is the in-flight-throw counter. Recorded here because `std::uncaught_exception` (`0x794AE9`) is nothing but a jump to it and cannot be read without it. No arguments, bare `ret`, `bool` in al.
addresses.evidence: The body is four instructions at `0xB9CD77`-`0xB9CD87`, read directly; it takes no arguments and ends in a bare `ret` with al set from a comparison against zero, so the signature is decidable. `0x7A0FFE` has 59 direct callers, which is the shape of a CRT per-thread-data accessor rather than anything game-specific. `inferred` because the name and the meaning of `+0x90` come from matching the CRT's `__uncaught_exception` / `__processing_throw` from memory. What would show it wrong: `0x7A0FFE` returning something other than a per-thread block - it is on the frontier and has not been read here.

addresses.name: std::locale::Destruct
addresses.comment:
Confirms the handover's reading of the body, with one correction to the name's spelling. This is `std::locale::~locale()` with `facet::_Decref()` inlined into it:

    if (_Ptr) {                       // the _Locimp* at locale +0
        _Lockit lock(_LOCK_LOCALE);   // 0x79504A with the literal 0
        if (0 < _Ptr->_Myrefs && _Ptr->_Myrefs != (size_t)-1) --_Ptr->_Myrefs;
        dead = _Ptr->_Myrefs == 0 ? _Ptr : 0;   // the neg/sbb/not/and at 0x42EE69
        ~_Lockit();                   // 0x795072
        if (dead) dead->vftable[0](1);          // scalar deleting destructor
    }

So a `locale` is one pointer wide, which is why `ios_base::_Init` allocates exactly four bytes into `_Ploc`; the refcount is at `_Locimp +4`; and `-1` is the sentinel that keeps the classic locale alive forever.

`__thiscall`, no stack arguments, bare `ret`. Four callers: `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` (`0x794BAE`), which destroys `_Ploc` at `+0x30` and then frees it, and three in `0x50E742`/`0x50ED2E`/`0x50ED54`.

**The name is spelled `Destruct`, not `~locale`.** project.json holds exactly one `~` name (`CSubUnitDataBase::~CSubUnitDataBase`) and the convention the log family already established for this is a word - `LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct`, `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor`. Whoever prefers the tilde should rename it once, everywhere.
addresses.evidence:
Mechanical: the body is 23 instructions at `0x42EE40`-`0x42EE8A`, `this` in ecx, no `[ebp+N]` read, bare `ret`. The `neg esi; sbb esi,esi; not esi; and esi,edi` sequence is the branchless `refs == 0 ? this : 0`, and the tail `mov eax,[esi]; mov edx,[eax]; push 1; mov ecx,esi; call edx` is a scalar deleting destructor called with the free flag. `0x79504A` and `0x795072` bracket the refcount update and are the same pair `std::ios_base::_Addstd` uses. The size claim is cross-checked: `std::ios_base::_Init` (already recorded) allocates four bytes for `_Ploc`.

`inferred` because the name rests on matching `<xlocale>`'s `locale::~locale` / `facet::_Decref` from memory. Two corroborations short of proof: the type descriptor `.?AV_Locimp@locale@std@@` is present in the image at `0x16F5220`, so the class this manages exists here under that name; and the `!= -1` test is the `_Locimp::_Clocptr` sentinel that only a locale refcount has. What would show it wrong: `[this]` pointing at something whose `+4` is not a refcount - the three non-`ios_base` callers at `0x50E742`, `0x50ED2E` and `0x50ED54` have not been read here.

addresses.name: std::_Lockit::_Lockit
addresses.evidence:
Mechanical: `imul eax,eax,0x18; add eax,0x174C878; push eax; call 0xB958D8` under `cmp eax,4`, and `0xB958D8` is `push [ebp+8]; call dword ptr [0xD2B120]; ret`, whose import name bytes read `EnterCriticalSection`. So the four-entry critical-section array and the bound are read off the executable, as is `ret 4` with `this` in ecx and `mov eax,esi` before the return.

`inferred` because the class name `_Lockit` and the `_MAX_LOCK` / `_LOCK_LOCALE` / `_LOCK_STREAM` spellings come from matching `<xlock>` from memory. What would show it wrong: the array at `0x174C878` being entered by something that is not this pair - `findRefs --address 0x174C878` finds four references, two of them the `imul` sites here and in the destructor and one the initialiser at `0xB95005`.

addresses.name: std::_Lockit::Destruct
addresses.comment:
The matching `~_Lockit()`: read the kind back out of `+0` and, if it is below 4, leave the same critical section. `0xB958E8` forwards to the `LeaveCriticalSection` import. Seven instructions, no prologue at all - `this` in ecx, no stack arguments, bare `ret`, nothing returned. 47 callers, the same count as the constructor.

Spelled `Destruct` rather than `~_Lockit` for the same reason as `std::locale::Destruct` above.
addresses.evidence: Mechanical: `mov eax,[ecx]; cmp eax,4; jge out; imul eax,eax,0x18; add eax,0x174C878; push eax; call 0xB958E8; pop ecx; ret` - the exact mirror of the constructor with the import at `0xD2B11C`, whose name bytes read `LeaveCriticalSection`. Bare `ret` with `this` in ecx and no `[ebp+N]` read fixes the convention. `inferred` for the name only, on the same grounds as the constructor. What would show it wrong: a caller that reaches it with something other than a `_Lockit` built by `0x79504A` - the caller lists are the same length and the two inspected pairs (`0x42EE50`/`0x42EE72` in `std::locale::Destruct`, `0x432338`/`0x432359`) bracket properly.

addresses.name: std::stringbuf::str
addresses.evidence:
(1) `findRefs --callers 0x00920940` returns exactly two, `0x91FB61` and `0xA5BD21`; the second is inside `std::ostringstream::str`, which project.json already records, and which reaches this by `add ecx,4` - the stringbuf inside the stream. (2) The two fields at `+0x3C` and `+0x40` are the two that `std::ostringstream::ostringstream` (already `confirmed`) writes at `stream+0x40` and `stream+0x44` with the stringbuf based at `stream+4`; the offsets agree exactly, which is a machine-checkable cross-reference between two independently reversed functions. (3) `esi` has no `push`/`pop` and no assignment anywhere in `0x920940`-`0x920A43`, and the last instruction before the bare `ret` is `mov eax,esi`, so it is an argument, not a saved register. (4) `0xA160` is already recorded as `std::string::assign(this, char*, len)` and is called with (pointer, length) computed from the buffer, and the `[out+0x14]=0xF` tidy is project.json's own `Hoi3CString` shape.

What would show it wrong: a third caller that does not set `esi` before the call (there are only two, both do); the `+0x3C`/`+0x40` pair not lining up with the ostringstream constructor's writes; or the two pointer-to-pointer indirections at `+0x14`/`+0x24` turning out to be single pointers, which would make the length arithmetic nonsense. The name's soft edge is `_Constant`/`_Noread` - those bit names come from `<sstream>` read from memory, though the *behaviour* (skip the put area on bit 1, skip the get area on bit 2) is read off the branches.

addresses.name: std::ios_base::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.comment:
Confirms the handover in full. MSVC's `??_G` for `ios_base`, and **the virtual-table slot that `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` (`0x794BAE`) sits behind**:

    mov  [esi], 0x15A7B8C        ; the ios_base vftable
    push esi; call 0x794BAE; add esp,4
    if (flags & 1) free(esi);
    return esi;

`__thiscall`, `ret 4`, the object back in eax. **It has no direct callers at all** - every use is a virtual dispatch, which is what one expects of a slot-0 destructor and is the complement of `_Ios_base_dtor`'s 700 direct calls.

**It is slot 0 of two tables**: `std::ios_base`'s own (`0x15A7B8C`, RTTI `.?AVios_base@std@@`) and `std::basic_ios<char>`'s (`0x15A7B9C`, RTTI `.?AV?$basic_ios@DU?$char_traits@D@std@@@std@@`, which project.json spells `std::anon::anon::std::D::DU__char_traits::__basic_ios`). Both tables have exactly one slot. The body belongs to `ios_base` - it writes `ios_base`'s own vftable, not `basic_ios`'s - and `basic_ios` derives from `ios_base` in project.json's class record, so the derived table holds the inherited body. Both slots are recorded under `vftable_slots`.

The neighbouring vftable `0x15A7B94` is `std::basic_ostream<char>`'s at object offset 8 and its slot 0 is a different body (`0x50E270`), so it is not part of this and is left on the frontier.
addresses.evidence:
Mechanical throughout. (1) `vtable.py --holding 0x00402210` returns exactly two tables, `std::ios_base` slot 0 and the `basic_ios<char>` class slot 0 - two, not the eight-plus that would mean a folded body. (2) The constant it writes, `0x15A7B8C`, is the table whose RTTI type descriptor reads `.?AVios_base@std@@`, which is why the body is `ios_base`'s and not the derived class's. (3) `test byte ptr [ebp+8],1` before `call 0x795F9B` (already recorded as `free`) is the textbook scalar-deleting-destructor flag, and the only other call is `0x794BAE`, already recorded as `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor`. (4) `ret 4` with `this` in ecx; `findRefs --callers` finds zero direct calls, consistent with a slot reached only by dispatch.

What would show it wrong: a third table holding it, or `0x15A7B8C` not being `ios_base`'s table. **What is not settled** is why `basic_ios<char>`'s slot 0 is this exact body rather than a `basic_ios`-specific one that writes `0x15A7B9C`: either the linker folded two identical bodies, or the compiler never emitted a distinct `??_Gbasic_ios` because `~basic_ios` is trivial and adds nothing. Nothing in the image distinguishes the two, and the difference does not change what the slot does.

slots_noted: Only 0x2210 is in a virtual table, and both of its tables are recorded above. `vtable.py --holding` reports 'in no class's virtual table' for 0x00B94A6E, 0x00B95991, 0x00B94AE9, 0x00B94AEE, 0x0042EE40, 0x00B9504A, 0x00B95072, 0x00920940 and 0x00B9CD77 - the constructors, the destructor bodies and the lock helpers are all called directly. std::locale::Destruct is worth singling out: it is a non-virtual destructor that *invokes* a virtual one (slot 0 of the _Locimp it holds), so it is a caller of a table, not a member of one.

notes:
THREE THINGS THE NEXT PERSON SHOULD NOT HAVE TO REDISCOVER.

1. `0x920940` IS A VIRTUAL ADDRESS, NOT AN RVA. The brief and the log-textbuilder
   handover both say 'rva 0x920940' for basic_stringbuf::str. The real rva is 0x520940;
   0x920940 is what disasm.py printed inside std::ostringstream::str, because disasm.py
   prints virtual addresses. Rva 0x920940 = VA 0xD20940 is not a function entry - it
   decodes from mid-instruction and findRefs finds no calls to it. The previous wave's
   own `frontier` list had it right as 0x520940; only the prose carried the VA.

2. WHAT WAS REFUTED. 'The two halves of building the std::ios_base::failure that
   ios_base::clear throws' is not what 0x794A6E and 0x795991 are.
   - 0x794A6E builds nothing. It is `std::iostream_category()`, two instructions
     answering the address of a static singleton, and what ios_base::clear does with it
     is store it as the `_Cat` half of the error_code the exception carries.
   - 0x795991 is the base constructor of *every* standard exception in the image, with
     297 callers; three of them happen to be ios_base::clear. Nothing in it is specific
     to `failure` - the caller writes the failure vftable and the error_code afterwards.
   The throw itself is confirmed, though, and more precisely than the handover put it:
   ios_base::clear throws `ios_base::failure("ios_base::badbit set" | "...failbit..." |
   "...eofbit...", make_error_code(io_errc::stream))`, vftable 0x15A7BD8, ThrowInfo
   0x164B158.

   Everything else the handover reported was confirmed as described: 0x794AE9 is a jump
   thunk to the CRT's __uncaught_exception at 0x79CD77, 0x794AEE is ios_base::_Callfns,
   0x2EE40 is locale's destructor, 0x79504A/0x795072 are _Lockit's constructor and
   destructor, and 0x2210 is the ios_base scalar deleting destructor with ret 4, the
   0x15A7B8C vftable write and the flag-bit free.

3. TWO THINGS checkSignatures WILL SAY ABOUT THIS FILE, BOTH EXPECTED.
   `std::iostream_category` and `std::uncaught_exception` take no arguments, so
   carriesClass() will list them under 'member functions whose signature never mentions
   their class'. They are not members - `std` is a namespace, not a class, and
   checkSignatures has no way to tell the two apart. The alternative was to drop the
   `std::` and lose the namespace, or to invent a parameter, and neither is worth it.
   The `ret` check itself agrees for all ten entries (0, 4, -, 0, 4, 0, 4, 0, 0, 4).
   std::uncaught_exception is the dash: it is a bare `jmp` with no `ret` of its own, so
   checkSignatures reports it as skipped, 'no ret reached - a tail jmp'. The jump target
   0x79CD77 is landed alongside it and does end in a bare `ret`, which is the check.

   Two destructors are spelled `Destruct` rather than `~locale` / `~_Lockit`:
   project.json holds exactly one tilde name, and the convention this family already set
   is a word (LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct, std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor). If the tilde
   is preferred, it is one rename in one place rather than two spellings in circulation.

WHAT COULD NOT BE SETTLED.
   - Why std::basic_ios<char>'s vftable slot 0 holds ios_base's body (0x2210) rather
     than one writing its own table 0x15A7B9C. Linker folding and a never-emitted
     trivial ??_Gbasic_ios both explain it and nothing in the image separates them.
   - The names `_Callfns`, `_Lockit`, `_MAX_LOCK`, `_Constant`/`_Noread`, `_Decref` and
     `__uncaught_exception` are header matches from memory, which is why those entries
     are `inferred`. Every one of them would be settled by compiling the corresponding
     MSVC header at the same optimisation level and comparing bytes; none of them was.

     0x50ED54) were not read, so the claim that its receiver is always a locale rests on
